summary: Paul W. Kroll studied sinology and linguistics at the University of Michigan (~1967–1976). He held posts at the University of Colorado Boulder as Associate Professor and department chairman (~1979–1989), in ~1989, and as a Faculty Fellow (attested 2001).

Paul Williams studied at the University of Sussex (~1969–1972) and Oxford/Wadham College (~1972–1978). In Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies, he was a visiting professor at the University of Calgary (~1996–1997) and department head at Bristol (attested 1998–2016).

Paula Kane Robinson Arai studied at Kalamazoo College (~1979–1983) and Harvard (~1985–1993) under Masatoshi Nagatomi and Wilfred Cantwell Smith. A scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology, she taught at Vanderbilt (~1994–2002) and Louisiana State University (~2007–2020).

Pe Maung Tin, a scholar of Buddhist studies, linguistics, and Indology, studied at the University of Yangon (~1904–1908) and the University of Calcutta (~1909–1911). He served as Professor of Pali at the University of Yangon (~1912–1946).
Pedro Manuel Castro Sánchez is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned his MA at the University of Sunderland, studying under Peter Harvey.

Pei-jung Wu studied at National Taiwan University and UCLA (Ph.D. by 2002), working under Donald F. McCallum, Hironobu Kohara, Shou-chien Shih, and Yu-min Lee. Her fields are history/archaeology, Japanology, and Buddhist studies.
Peipei Qiu, a specialist in Japanology and sinology, studied at Peking University and Columbia University, where she studied under Paul Rouzer. She held a post at Vassar College (attested 2005).

Pema Bhum works in Tibetology. He is a former professor of Tibetan languages and letters at Lanzhou University and Indiana University, and served as Director of the Latse Contemporary Tibetan Cultural Library (attested 2003–2009).

Pema Chödrön works in Buddhist studies. She studied at Miss Porter's School and UC Berkeley Graduate School of Education, and studied under traditional teachers Chögyam Trungpa, Dzigar Kongtrul Rinpoche, and Sakyong Mipham.

Penghao Sun works in Tibetology and history/archaeology. He studied under doctoral supervisor Leonard van der Kuijp, as well as teachers Qingying Chen (2009–2011), Mark C. Elliott, Charles Hallisey, Peter K. Bol, Jay Jasanoff, James Robson, Ryuichi Abe, Jie Li, and Weirong Shen.
Pentti Aalto was a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Helsinki (~1934–1949) and held a post there from ~1958 to 1980.

Per Kjeld Sørensen studied at the University of Copenhagen (~1971–1981) under Erik Haarh (~1975–1985). Active in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, he held posts at Copenhagen (~1981–1994), the University of Bonn (1991–1992), and Leipzig University (1995).

Per Kvaerne earned his Ph.D. at the University of Oslo (~1970–1973). In Tibetology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies, he was a professor at the University of Oslo (~1975–2007) and Secretary General of the International Association for Tibetan Studies (~1989–1995).
Perry Link studied sinology and linguistics at Harvard University (~1962–1976). He held academic posts at Princeton University (~1989–2008) and the University of California, Riverside (~2008).

Perry Schmidt-Leukel works in religious studies, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He held posts at LMU Munich (~1988–1998), the University of Salzburg (~1998–1999), the University of Glasgow (~1999–2009), the University of Münster (~2009–2020), and the University of Innsbruck.
Peter Alan Roberts is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teacher Khenchen Thrangu Rinpoche in 1979 and doctoral supervisor Michael Aris.

Peter Bisschop studied Indology at the University of Groningen (PhD -2004) under Hans T. Bakker and Harunaga Isaacson. He was a Junior Research Fellow at Wolfson College, Oxford, Lecturer at Edinburgh (2005–2010), and Editor at Leiden (attested 2011–2021).
Peter Connolly studied religious studies and Indology at Lancaster University (BA, MA, Ph.D.). He held a post at the University of Chichester as Lecturer in Religious Studies in 1980.

Peter D. Hershock studied philosophy and Buddhist studies at Yale University and with traditional teachers Seungsahn and Ji Kwang Dae Poep Sa Nim. He directed the Asian Studies Development Program at the East-West Center (attested 2007–2013).
Peter Ebbatson is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned his PhD at the University of Oxford, where he studied under doctoral supervisor Walpola Rahula.
